text:
sara: Alert: we're seeing a burst of SSO session revokes for ~120 accounts across multiple tenants in the last 10m. Many users report repeated MFA push prompts then session drop. IP clusters: 52.37.11.0/24 and 34.120.9.0/24. Possible MFA-prompt flood or automated replay. I'm escalating.

kai: Do we know if revokes originated from our side (token revocation API) or the IdP?

okta-bot: Okta detection: automated "unusual activity" rule triggered for app 'redwood-prod'. Okta issued session revokes for affected sessions at 1966123402-1966123450.

maria: Copy. Any signs of credential stuffing (many failed password attempts) in auth logs?

sara: Auth logs show high rate of authentication attempts from same IP clusters, some succeeded (valid creds), many triggered push MFA. Timing is suspicious: bursts every ~30s.

julian: Recommend immediate containment: block the two IP ranges at edge + add rate-limit on SSO callback endpoints. Also rotate the app client secret and pause non-essential service accounts.

infra-bot: Applied temporary firewall rules to block 52.37.11.0/24 and 34.120.9.0/24 at the perimeter (rule id fw-block-1966). Added emergency rate limit for /api/sso/callback to 50 req/min.

sara: Thanks infra. @maria please coordinate customer comms for affected tenants (email + status page). QA: don't rotate their keys yet until we confirm impact.

maria: Will draft notice. Asking product for scope list — which tenants saw >5 revokes.

kai: I'm pulling token issuance logs and KMS usage for last 24h to check suspicious key access. If we rotated client secret, we need to ensure KMS manifests updated before app restart.

julian: Steps: 1) Block IPs (done) 2) Pause problematic service accounts 3) Rotate client secret (prepare but don't deploy) 4) Re-enable after verification 5) Postmortem and IOCs.

sara: Also flag this for potential MFA fatigue attack. Can we change push behavior temporarily (require biometric on push or send number challenge)?

kai: Not quick to change Okta MFA config across orgs. Short-term: enable push throttling via our SSO proxy (already added).

maria: Drafted comms and status page update: "We're investigating elevated MFA prompts and session interruptions; containment in progress." Sending to legal & trust for review.

oncall-rotation: I'm on it, running the revoke-check script now and will list affected users in this thread.

infra-bot: Revoke-check output (top lines):
```
1966123421 user=alice@tenantA action=revoke src=52.37.11.12
1966123423 user=bob@tenantB action=revoke src=34.120.9.21
1966123430 user=svc-dataflow action=force-logout src=52.37.11.45
```

kai: Found three service accounts with suspicious token refreshes. I'm suspending them and creating tickets 9876,9877.

sara: Good. Also open an Okta support request and request their telemetry for those IPs.

okta-bot: Okta ticket created: OKTA-54211. Okta advised revoking sessions for affected users and rotating compromised app credentials.

julian: After containment, schedule a post-incident conference call and assign a short RCA owner. I'll take the RCA if no objections.

maria: Notifying SOC customers and posting preliminary incident note on status.redwood.com.

sara: Action items recap: [infra] block IPs & keep rate limits, [kai] suspend suspicious service accounts + gather logs, [maria] customer comms & legal review, [julian] prepare client secret rotation plan (hold), [oncall] compile affected user list. We'll reconvene in 30m. :thumbsup:

oncall-rotation: Affected user list coming in ~5m.

sara: Thanks everyone. Keep thread live for updates. We'll lock down final mitigations after Okta telemetry & KMS access review.
